about: Every word rule Msetter's interface, pages, docs and Mac app are checked against, by test/voice.test.js. The voice part is copied from the house voice rules by tools/sync_voice.py; edit the rest by hand. Patterns are JavaScript regular expressions; ci means ignore case.

voice.about: From the house voice rules' verification grep, by tools/sync_voice.py. Do not edit by hand.

voice_skipped.scolding: about the owner's own work cadence; the app never reports on it
voice_skipped.passive voice: a first net for prose; too many fixed phrases in docs (is saved, is reset) to fail a build on
voice_skipped.hedges: first-person hedges; the first-person check covers them
voice_skipped.preamble tells: letters and briefings; framing sentences are read by hand
voice_skipped.lead-ins, asides, second names: Markdown lead-ins are read by hand; "the body" is a project pattern
voice_skipped.every, as emphasis: a list to read, not a failure: the agreed labels say "every profile"; the project page and README check fails on it there

struck.about: Phrases struck from the page in review. Never again, anywhere a person reads. Matched ignoring case.

retired.about: One word for one thing. In interface text (src/*.js strings, index.html, mac/*.swift) and the public pages (README.md, site/index.html, the issue templates) the word on the left is retired; use the one on the right. The docs may still use a technical word where they define it. Matched as written, at word edges.

words.Your design: the starting point's own name: Factory, the set's name, From your camera
words.Unnamed setting: A setting Msetter can't name yet
words.Film Mode: the row's own name (Contrast, Sharpness, Saturation)
words.Click: nothing: the label is the verb
words.Double-click: nothing: the label is the verb
words.Tap: nothing: the label is the verb
words.Drag to: nothing: the label is the verb
words.Drag a number: nothing: the label is the verb
words.Point at: nothing: the label is the verb
words.Hover: nothing: the label is the verb

spelling.about: American spelling, because the app quotes Leica's English names and those are American. British stem on the left, American on the right; a word that starts with the stem fails.

project.about: The project's own patterns, from the writing rules and design rule 6. Everywhere a person reads. Edit by hand.

unknowns as a schedule.re: not yet (confirmed|checked|tested|tried|known)|not known yet|hasn.t been (tried|tested|checked)|no clue yet

idiom headings.re: ^#+ (What about|Where it stands|What it would take|Who else|Why not)|>What about the Q<|\[What about the Q\]

ui_only.about: Interface text only (src/*.js strings, index.html, mac/*.swift): labels, not explanations (design rule 6).

allow.about: Phrases a pattern above would catch but which are right where they are: genre and set names, other people's quoted words (matched ignoring case). Strings: whole interface strings that stay as they are, with the reason.

strings.Click: the pretend camera's toast for the shutter sound
